There are trains, and men on them, and each individual departure is a private decision that nobody has the authority to prevent. The front is not broken. It is vacated.The front · 28 November 1917Expand the mapGumbinnenKonigsbergLembergLembergPetrogradBaranovichiLvovGorliceBerdichevPskovTarnopolMogilev-7MANPOWER ▾-7MUNITIONS ▾-10HOME STABILITY ▾Contested judgmentAn army is an agreement about who gives orders. Once that agreement lapses, nothing in the field replaces it. What actually happened: The front did dissolve. Desertion had been heavy since the summer, and after the revolution of October the armistice signed at Brest-Litovsk on 2 December (15 December in the west) only recognised what had occurred. The old army was demobilised by decree over the winter of 1917 and 1918, and the men went home. Nobody knows how many deserted, and the figures that are given are estimates made by people who had reasons to make them large or small.
